definition: O'Connor's own metaethics (2023): moral statements are expressions of emotion ('murder, boo'), with a prescriptive element ('don't murder'), and have no truth value at all; he calls it a form of ethical non-cognitivism. Only the denial of truth value is formalized (`MoralStatementsLackTruthValueReading`).
